testsrc_1s.mp4 was generated with:

ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=s=64x64:d=1 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart testsrc_1s.mp4

testsrc_1s_recompressed.mp4 was generated from the same lavfi source at a
different quality setting (crf 35 instead of the default), to simulate a
real re-encode with the same visual content but different bytes/bitrate:

ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=s=64x64:d=1 -c:v libx264 -crf 35 -pix_fmt yuv420p -movflags +faststart testsrc_1s_recompressed.mp4

A 1-second, 64x64, structured test-pattern clip (gradients + a moving box,
not a flat color) used by the video near-duplicate-detection tests. Unlike
`red_1s.mp4` (a flat solid-red frame, whose dHash is degenerately all-zero
bits since a flat frame has no left>right pixel transitions anywhere),
`testsrc2` produces a poster-frame with real structure, so its dHash
actually discriminates: measured Hamming distance between `testsrc_1s.mp4`
and `red_1s.mp4`'s dHash is 23 (correctly judged NOT similar, threshold 10),
while the distance between `testsrc_1s.mp4` and its own recompressed
variant is 2 (correctly judged similar despite different bytes/bitrate;
this is the actual near-duplicate scenario the feature targets: same
source, different encoding).

ffmpeg is not a project dependency. It was only used once, locally, to
produce these two committed fixtures. Regenerate with the commands above if
either fixture ever needs to change.
